ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the quadrilateral $ABCD$ is inscribed in circle $\odot O$, with $\angle BCD = 105^\circ$. What is the measure of $\angle BOD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that quadrilateral ABCD is inscribed in circle O,\\
it follows that $\angle A + \angle BCD = 180^\circ$,\\
therefore $\angle A = 180^\circ - \angle BCD = 180^\circ - 105^\circ = 75^\circ$,\\
hence $\angle BOD = 2\angle A = 2 \times 75^\circ = \boxed{150^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a circle, with the center of the circle labeled O; the four points A, B, C, D are all on the circumference, forming the cyclic quadrilateral ABCD. The radii OB and OD are also drawn in the figure, therefore ∠BOD is a central angle formed by two radii. The problem gives ∠BCD = 105°. Reasoning: Because ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral, opposite angles are supplementary, ∠BAD + ∠BCD = 180°. Therefore ∠BAD = 180° - 105° = 75°. ∠BAD is the inscribed angle subtending chord BD, and ∠BOD is the central angle subtending the same chord BD. According to the central angle being equal to 2 times the inscribed angle subtending the same arc, ∠BOD = 2 × 75° = 150°.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram: C lies on the lower arc between B and D, while the central angle ∠BOD shown by radii OB and OD is the smaller central angle over the lower/minor arc BD. From the text, ∠BCD = 105°. By the inscribed-angle theorem, ∠BCD intercepts the arc BD that does not contain C, namely the major arc from B through A to D, so that arc has measure 2 × 105° = 210°. The full circle is 360°, so the remaining minor arc BD has measure 360° - 210° = 150°. The central angle ∠BOD subtending that minor arc equals the arc measure, hence ∠BOD = 150°.
